Issued at 316 PM EDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast: Broad upper ridge encompasses roughly the 
southern half of the CONUS...save for a long wave trough that runs 
along the east coast.  A short wave trough coming over the top of 
the ridge and into the Midwest today will be a feature of interest 
heading into the weekend...a couple of smaller PV anomalies also 
coming over the top of the ridge across Idaho/Montana.  Low 
amplitude westerly flow across much of Canada...emanating from a 
long wave trough off the British Columbia coast. Anticyclonic upper 
level flow across the Great Lakes today with broadly difluent flow 
ahead of the Midwest short wave trough; also ahead of this trough is 
a narrow axis of deep layer moisture (precipitable water at or above 
2.00 inches spanning the Mississippi Valley).  Mid level deformation 
zone extends from eastern North Dakota/northern Minnesota/northwest 
Ontario.  At the surface...1006mb low along the Iowa/Minnesota 
border with a warm front extending southeast across Iowa and along 
the Mississippi River.  Cold front was north of Lake Superior into 
northern Minnesota.  Broad high pressure across the Ohio Valley and 
mid Atlantic region with several high centers including a 1016m high 
bubble over southern Lower Michigan.

Cold advection into the backside of the upper Midwest short wave 
trough suggests a continued digging and strengthening over the next 
24 hours...approaching a -3 sigma 500mb height anomaly across the 
mid Mississippi Valley.  This trough will slowly meander across the 
Ohio Valley this weekend...what happens beyond that is uncertain. 
Will this system track into the mid Atlantic Monday...will it hang 
on longer (slower is usually the better way to go)...or does the 
trough split and a piece gets left behind to drift into the 
southeast states early next week?  Questions about the evolution of 
this feature may not have much impact on the upper Lakes...provided 
we can get some height rises/surface high pressure into the region 
by Tuesday and the "piece gets left behind to drift into the 
southeast states" idea mentioned above gets slingshotted back in our 
direction instead.  Regardless...the trend should be toward more 
unsettle weather by midweek...as the trough currently over the 
northeast Pacific moves inland and takes up residence across central 
Canada. This should send height falls and a cold front into the 
Great Lakes around Wednesday. 

Primary Forecast Concerns: 

Widespread rain tonight/Saturday as a cool-season cyclone passes 
south of the Great Lakes.  Heavy rain threat parts of eastern 
Upper/northeast Lower this evening: Upstream system over southern 
Minnesota much more reminiscent of something we will be more 
familiar with in a couple of months rather than something we 
typically see in late July.  But it is there...with a nice 
deformation precipitation shield across southern Minnesota/northern 
Wisconsin...and a warm frontal rain band spreading northeast across 
southern Wisconsin. Meanwhile...at the onset this afternoon things 
are just starting to bubble up on the cloud front...with the Lake 
Huron breeze having kicked in north of Thunder Bay.  Across eastern 
Upper an uncapped MLCAPE 1000+J/kg... with lake breeze convection 
underway from Marquette to the Soo. Combination of afternoon 
convection...eastward extension of precipitation band across 
northern Wisconsin/western Upper...and the main precipitation shield 
wrapping around the upper midwest cyclone will be the impetus for 
rain across northern Michigan tonight and Saturday.  Given high 
precipitable water...K indices above 35...and light cloud layer flow 
there is concern for slow moving heavy downpours through midnight 
across eastern Upper and parts of northeast Lower and may carry an 
explicit heavy rain wording to cover this.  A lot of moisture around 
Saturday but not a lot of forcing...though southern portions of the 
forecast area will still be close to the main deformation zone.   

Drying out from north to south Sunday (though could be a slower 
process than we would like):  Rain chances should start to come to 
an end across eastern Upper and parts of northwest Lower Saturday 
night...but will continue into Sunday for about the southeast third 
of the forecast area.  Slow moving deformation zones can be stubborn 
in clearing out...so later forecasts may trend toward hanging onto 
some rain chances over (at least) northeast Lower for a bit longer. 
But expecting things to dry out all areas by Monday.

Rain chances return Wednesday: Height falls and a resultant cold 
front looks to cross the upper Lakes Tuesday night/Wednesday which 
will bring the next chance for showers and thunderstorms.  Outlook 
beyond Wednesday is a bit more uncertain...but removed a lot of 
spotty slight chance PoPs for Thursday/Friday for the time being.&&
